modules.title: Provenance: EXIF, C2PA, watermarks, generator metadata
modules.question: What does the file itself declare about where it came from, and what of that is cryptographically verified?

requirements.name: c2pa
requirements.how_to_enable: uv sync --extra provenance   (adds C2PA / Content Credentials checking)

requirements.name: imwatermark
requirements.how_to_enable: uv sync --extra provenance   (adds open invisible-watermark decoding)

limitations: Everything in EXIF/XMP is declared by the file and can be added, edited, copied or removed by anyone.
Missing metadata is normal: WhatsApp, Instagram, X, Facebook and most platforms strip it. Absence is Unknown, never evidence of authenticity or of manipulation.
A C2PA signature proves who signed a record and that the file is unchanged since; the signer's statements are only as honest as the signer.
Proprietary watermarks (SynthID and others) have no public detector and were not checked.
A phone or camera model identifies a model shared by millions of devices, never one device.

validation.summary: Parsing of EXIF/C2PA/watermark data is deterministic and covered by unit tests; no statistical method is involved. Attribution tiers follow reasoning/generator.py.

modules.title: PRNU sensor-noise fingerprinting
modules.question: Could this image have been captured by one of the candidate cameras whose reference photos are on file?

requirements.name: pywt
requirements.how_to_enable: uv sync   (PyWavelets is a core dependency)

limitations: It tests a specific suspected camera; it never identifies a camera on its own.
A camera model is not a device: only reference photos from the suspected physical device can support a match.
The pattern is weakened or destroyed by resizing, cropping, heavy JPEG compression, screenshots and platform re-encoding; the image must have the same pixel size and orientation as the references.
AI-generated images carry no sensor pattern, and a non-match proves nothing about authenticity.
Validated on simulated sensors only; no real-camera test set has been run.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated sensors with known fixed-pattern noise. NOT validated on real cameras: no labelled real-camera set was available.
validation.dataset: 8 simulated devices x 10 reference images, 6 test images per device, 512 px, 13 transformations

modules.title: Camera-processing fingerprints
modules.question: Does the pixel data carry the traces of a camera-style processing chain (demosaicing, sharpening, sensor noise, lens, JPEG)?
limitations: These traces describe processing, not origin: a camera, a RAW converter and some image synthesis can all produce them.
Resizing, screenshots, heavy JPEG compression and social-media re-encoding erase demosaicing and noise traces. A missing trace is mostly Unknown.
No camera make or model can be derived from these measurements.
Thresholds were set on simulated sensors; behaviour on real cameras has not been measured.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated sensors (bilinear demosaicing, known sharpening / denoising / chromatic aberration). Real camera pipelines (proprietary demosaicing, HDR, AI denoising) are not covered.

cfa.note: Detection survives JPEG down to roughly quality 90-95 on simulated bilinear demosaicing; it is erased by any resizing.

validation.dataset: Simulated Bayer sensors with known processing

modules.title: Editing and recompression analysis
modules.question: Is there any sign that parts of the image were processed differently from the rest, resized, recompressed or copied?
limitations: Every cue here also fires on innocent processing (screenshots, platform recompression, resizing, filters). Treat flags as leads for visual review.
A clean result does not show authenticity: careful edits, fully generated images and regions processed with the whole image leave none of these traces.
Localisation boxes are tile-based (64 px) and approximate.

Measured on simulated edits: splices whose compression history differs from the rest of the picture are localised; splices pasted before a single JPEG save, and rescaled pastes, are largely missed. See the validation results.
Thresholds were set on simulated edits; the false-positive rate on real web photos is reported in the validation results.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated splices, copy-move, resizing and double compression, plus a false-positive measurement on real web photographs.

modules.title: Video acquisition analysis
modules.question: How was this video recorded and processed: frame timing, codec and container, camera motion and rolling shutter?

requirements.name: ffprobe
requirements.how_to_enable: Install FFmpeg and add it to PATH

requirements.name: ffmpeg
requirements.how_to_enable: Install FFmpeg and add it to PATH

limitations: Frame timing and container facts describe the file as received. Platforms re-encode uploads, which rewrites all of them.
Rolling-shutter and stabilisation estimates need real camera movement; a tripod shot or a still scene gives Unknown.
Codec traces show the LAST encoder, not the original capture device.
Motion-based estimates were validated on simulated video only; no real camera footage has been measured.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated panning video with known rolling-shutter read-out, frame drops/duplicates and encoders. No real camera footage was measured.

modules.title: Audio forensics
modules.question: What does the audio say about the recording environment and chain, and does it stay in step with the picture?

requirements.name: ffmpeg
requirements.how_to_enable: Install FFmpeg and add it to PATH

requirements.name: yunet
requirements.how_to_enable: uv run python ../scripts/setup_models.py yunet   (needed for audio/video sync)

limitations: These measurements describe the recording and its processing; none of them says whether a voice is genuine. No voice-clone classifier is bundled.
Lossy codecs, noise reduction and platform re-encoding (WhatsApp voice notes, social video) change hum, noise floor and reverberation estimates.
Reverberation is a blind estimate from speech decays and tends to under-read in dry rooms.
Audio/video sync needs a visible talking face for at least 8 s; otherwise it is Unknown.
Estimators were validated on simulated audio and video only.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated speech with known hum, reverberation, clipping, noise floors and audio/video offsets. No real recordings were measured.
